answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must bind identities into cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Clustering agents requires staking bonding capital that scales superlinearly; an attacker attempting to simulate a knoll of independent nodes across an orchard of validator clusters quickly faces exponential capital exhaustion. When fraudulent nodes mimic a willow bending under network auditing, their staked bonds slash exponentially, pricing out swarms.
